info.title: dreamDEX WebSocket API
info.description:
WebSocket API for dreamDEX, providing real-time market data
through subscription-based channels and REST-over-WebSocket RPC.

Use `subscribe` and `unsubscribe` operations to manage channel subscriptions.
Invoke any REST API endpoint over the socket by its OpenAPI operationId with a
`RestRequest`; responses arrive as `RestResponse` and may be out of order, so
correlate by `id`.

Send `{"operation": "ping"}` to receive a `pong`; an idle connection is closed
after 60 seconds (close code `1000`). On server shutdown the connection is closed
with `1001` — reconnect and resubscribe.

public.title: Public Market Data
public.description:
Primary WebSocket channel for real-time market data. Clients connect to this
channel to receive order book updates, OHLCV candles, trade executions, and
order status changes. All communication uses JSON messages.

receivePing.description: The server replies immediately with a pong. Send pings periodically to keep the connection from timing out after 60s of inactivity.

receiveSubscribe.description: The server validates the params and, on success, replies with a subscribed confirmation, then the feed's current state — an initial snapshot for the book/candle/trade channels, or a replay of recent lifecycle events for the order channels — followed by incremental updates as data changes.

receiveUnsubscribe.description: The server stops sending updates for the feed and replies with an unsubscribed confirmation.

receiveRestRequest.description: Invoke a REST endpoint by its OpenAPI operationId; the server runs it through the HTTP handler and replies with a RestResponse. `operation` is the operationId itself (e.g. `GetMarkets`), matched case-insensitively; `params` fills the path and then the query, every value sent as a string.

sendPong.description: Reply to a ping; confirms the connection is alive and resets the inactivity timeout. Echoes back the client's `clientTimestamp` when one was sent, so the client can measure round-trip latency.

sendSubscribed.description: Confirms a subscription; echoes back the subscription params so the client can verify which feed was activated.

sendUnsubscribed.description: Confirms an unsubscription. After this frame no further updates are sent for the feed.

sendError.description: A subscription-path request could not be processed — invalid params, unknown channel, or a server-side issue. `message` is human-readable.

sendProtocolError.description: A REST-over-WebSocket request could not be processed for protocol reasons (unknown operation, missing params, overload). Distinct from HTTP errors, which are returned inside a RestResponse. `id` echoes the request when it carried a valid integer id.

sendShutdown.description: Broadcast to all clients before the server terminates connections on graceful shutdown. Reconnect (to another server) or retry after a delay.

sendRestResponse.description: The result of a REST request: HTTP status and body. `id` matches the request for correlation; responses may arrive out of order, so correlate by `id`.

sendOrderbookSnapshot.description: The complete order book on subscribe. Bids are sorted by price descending (highest first), asks ascending (lowest first). Initialize local state from this before applying updates. An event-contract market's book is in YES terms (a NO bid at 1 - p is a YES ask at p); once the market is finalized or its pool hosts the next market, a final update clears every level and the subscription goes quiet.

sendOrderbookUpdate.description: Incremental order book changes: changed levels in `bids` and/or `asks`, each present only when it has changes. A quantity of zero means the level was removed; otherwise replace the quantity at that price.

sendStreamEnd.description: Sent once on an event-contract market's `orderbook`, `ohlcv` or `trades` subscription when the market is finalized or its pool hosts the next market, even when nothing else changed. Nothing follows it: unsubscribe, and subscribe to the next market. Spot and perp streams never send it. An event market can't be subscribed to before its trading start: until then its pool may still be serving the market before it.

sendOHLCVSnapshot.description: Historical candles on subscribe, for the requested symbol and timeframe. Populate charts from this before live updates. An event-contract market's candles are its own, priced as the YES probability, and fold only fills timestamped inside its trading window (tradingStart to expiry): a late-delivered fill from before expiry still counts, and nothing after it does.

sendOHLCVUpdate.description: A new or updated candle. If the timestamp matches an existing candle, replace it (still forming); a new timestamp means the previous candle closed.

sendTradesSnapshot.description: Recent trade history on subscribe, up to the requested limit (default 100), ordered by timestamp descending (newest first).

sendTradesUpdate.description: A single trade as it executes, with price, quantity, and aggressor side. `takerRemaining` and `makerRemaining` are each order's unfilled remainder after the fill (base units; `0` means the fill completed that order), so a partial fill is distinguishable from a complete one.

sendOrderUpdate.description: An event when the subscribed order changes: `placed`, `reduced`, `filled`, `cancelled`, `expired`. On subscribe the last ten minutes of the order's events are replayed (no separate snapshot); each update carries only the event-specific fields (e.g. `price`, `quantity`, `remaining`). On an event-contract market the order is stated in its owner's YES/NO terms (`outcome`, with `isBid` and `price` in that outcome's terms); events from before the market opened belong to an earlier market on the same pool and are not this order's, and updates stop once the market is finalized or its pool moves on.

sendFundingSnapshot.description: The pool's funding state on subscribe: the rate for the current calculation window, the running accumulator, and the index and mark prices behind them. Rates are 1e18-scaled fractions per funding CALCULATION WINDOW, exactly as the contract emits them — the same figures `GET /v0/markets/{symbol}/funding` reports as `current`. Perpetual markets only.

sendFundingUpdate.description: A funding settlement. Every field of the snapshot is carried, so replace the funding state wholesale rather than folding anything into it. `intervalsSettled` reports how many funding intervals the settlement covered, which is more than one when a pool has not been poked for a while.

sendLiquidationSnapshot.description: A market's recent liquidation legs on subscribe, newest first, up to the requested limit (default 100) — the same rows `GET /v0/markets/{symbol}/liquidations` serves. Perpetual markets only.

sendLiquidationUpdate.description: One pool-scoped leg of a liquidation as it happens. `kind` says which stage of the waterfall it is and should be read first — a forced deleveraging and an ordinary liquidation are otherwise indistinguishable. A leg already carried by the snapshot is suppressed by `id`, so a subscribe does not report the same leg twice.

sendMarketsSnapshot.description: On subscribe to `markets`: every live event-contract market on the chain, soonest expiry first, as the indexer lists them (`GET /v0/markets?kind=event` also leaves out one whose book grid can't be read, so the two can briefly differ). Follow an asset across rolls from here and the updates that follow, rather than polling the list.

sendMarketsUpdate.summary: An event-contract market was created, resolved or voided
sendMarketsUpdate.description: One lifecycle step of an event-contract market. `created`: a new market, ready to subscribe to once its `tradingStart` passes. `resolved`: its winning `outcome` and `payout`. `voided`: its `payout`, with no winner. A market's streams on the other channels end with a StreamEnd frame at the same point.

sendPositionsSnapshot.description: Your open perp positions on subscribe, one per market you hold a position in — the same rows `GET /v0/markets/{symbol}/positions/mine` serves. AUTHENTICATED: the subscribe frame must carry a valid bearer token in `params.bearerToken`, and the stream is bound to that token's wallet — you cannot subscribe to another wallet's positions. Perpetual markets only.

sendPositionsUpdate.description: One of your positions after it changed. `size`, `avgEntryPrice` and `realizedPnl` are the position's absolute new state, so replace the position wholesale rather than folding anything into it (a repeat carries the same state and is safe to reapply). A `size` of `0` means the position is closed — remove it from local state, the way a `0`-quantity order-book level is removed. The snapshot never carries a closed position (flat rows are excluded). Also emitted after a funding settlement or an auto-deleveraging on the position.

sendPendingOrderUpdate.description: A pending (stop) order lifecycle event: `pending_created`, `pending_triggered` (trigger reached; `success` reports whether a spot order was placed, with `spotOrderId` present on success), or `pending_cancelled`. Subscribe with the market symbol and order ID.

A re-read whose levels are unchanged emits nothing.
The frame carries the levels that changed, not the events that changed them.

lossy: Whether the market resolved or voided, and its payout, are not on this frame: read `GET /v0/markets/{symbol}`.

OHLCVSnapshot.name: OHLCVSnapshot
OHLCVSnapshot.title: OHLCV Snapshot
OHLCVSnapshot.description: Historical candles on subscribe, for the requested symbol and timeframe. Populate charts from this before live updates. An event-contract market's candles are its own, priced as the YES probability, and fold only fills timestamped inside its trading window (tradingStart to expiry): a late-delivered fill from before expiry still counts, and nothing after it does.

x-derived-from.from: read: the indexer's candles for the timeframe
lossy: A fill mined after the indexer's watermark but before the subscriber attached is replayed from the chain into the open bucket when it falls within the ten-minute replay window, except one whose maker was placed and filled in the same block: that maker left no resting state to read its side from, so that fill alone can still leave the bucket short.

The open bucket's candle history and the watermark it is folded past are two separate indexer reads, so a fill the indexer ingests between them is counted by neither for the life of that bucket - a bounded undercount on the order of the gap between the reads.

The chain replay and the live stream are folded as two ordered passes rather than one merged sequence, so around a bucket boundary a live fill the replay did not also return can arrive after the bucket has rolled and be left uncounted.

OHLCVUpdate.title: OHLCV Update
OHLCVUpdate.description: A new or updated candle. If the timestamp matches an existing candle, replace it (still forming); a new timestamp means the previous candle closed.

lossy: A fill whose maker order cannot be resolved is dropped without a frame and without a counter: dreamdex_fills_unresolved_total covers the REST mapper, not this path.
Buckets are folded, so the frame carries the open bucket's running state rather than the fill that moved it.

TradesSnapshot.description: Recent trade history on subscribe, up to the requested limit (default 100), ordered by timestamp descending (newest first).

lossy: A fill the indexer recorded with no taker side is omitted rather than reported with a guessed one, so the snapshot can be short of the requested limit.

TradesUpdate.title: Trades Update
TradesUpdate.description: A single trade as it executes, with price, quantity, and aggressor side. `takerRemaining` and `makerRemaining` are each order's unfilled remainder after the fill (base units; `0` means the fill completed that order), so a partial fill is distinguishable from a complete one.

lossy: A fill whose maker order cannot be resolved is dropped without a frame and without a counter: dreamdex_fills_unresolved_total covers the REST mapper, not this path.

The trade's side is the taker's, inferred from the maker's resting direction.

FundingUpdate.name: FundingUpdate
FundingUpdate.title: Funding Update
FundingUpdate.description: A funding settlement. Every field of the snapshot is carried, so replace the funding state wholesale rather than folding anything into it. `intervalsSettled` reports how many funding intervals the settlement covered, which is more than one when a pool has not been poked for a while.

lossy: Per-account settlement is not on this channel: FundingSettled is emitted by the MarginBank per account, and a per-market channel would publish every account's payment to every subscriber. Poll `GET /v0/markets/{symbol}/funding/mine` for a wallet's own payments.
A settlement mined while the snapshot was being read is suppressed when it describes the state the snapshot already carried, so it is delivered once or not at all.

LiquidationSnapshot.name: LiquidationSnapshot
LiquidationSnapshot.title: Liquidation Snapshot
LiquidationSnapshot.description: A market's recent liquidation legs on subscribe, newest first, up to the requested limit (default 100) — the same rows `GET /v0/markets/{symbol}/liquidations` serves. Perpetual markets only.

x-derived-from.from: read: the indexer's recent liquidation legs
lossy: Account-scoped stages of the waterfall name no market and are not carried: a subscriber sees the pool-scoped legs of a liquidate() call, not the call. AccountLiquidated, CloseOutMarginSettled, BadDebtAbsorbed and the residual/coverage stages are all account-scoped.

A leg the chain recorded with no size or no price is omitted rather than reported as zero, exactly as the REST endpoint omits it, so a liquidate() call can appear with fewer legs than the chain recorded.

LiquidationUpdate.name: LiquidationUpdate
LiquidationUpdate.title: Liquidation Update
LiquidationUpdate.description: One pool-scoped leg of a liquidation as it happens. `kind` says which stage of the waterfall it is and should be read first — a forced deleveraging and an ordinary liquidation are otherwise indistinguishable. A leg already carried by the snapshot is suppressed by `id`, so a subscribe does not report the same leg twice.

lossy: AutoDeleveraged is carried too but comes from the MarginBank, not this contract: the waterfall is split across both singletons.

LiquidationFeeCharged, LiquidationThrottled and LiquidationOrderPanicked are pool-scoped but not carried: the indexer records no row for them, so a snapshot could never reproduce one and a client would lose them silently on every reconnect.
PositionSkippedBelowMinQuantity, PositionTransferred and AdlCapacityShortfall are pool-scoped but carry no price, so they are dropped by the same rule the REST endpoint applies.
The LiquidationEngine and MarginBank watches are shared across every subscribed market, so a lapse in either is a gap for all of them at once.

MarketsSnapshot.title: Markets Snapshot
MarketsSnapshot.description: On subscribe to `markets`: every live event-contract market on the chain, soonest expiry first, as the indexer lists them (`GET /v0/markets?kind=event` also leaves out one whose book grid can't be read, so the two can briefly differ). Follow an asset across rolls from here and the updates that follow, rather than polling the list.

lossy: A point-in-time read: a market listed after it arrives as a `created` update.

MarketsUpdate.name: MarketsUpdate
MarketsUpdate.title: Markets Update
MarketsUpdate.summary: An event-contract market was created, resolved or voided
MarketsUpdate.description: One lifecycle step of an event-contract market. `created`: a new market, ready to subscribe to once its `tradingStart` passes. `resolved`: its winning `outcome` and `payout`. `voided`: its `payout`, with no winner. A market's streams on the other channels end with a StreamEnd frame at the same point.

also.from: event: MarketFinalized (the voided flag and payout)

lossy: A created market is named by the registry, which waits for the indexer to have it; one it still can't resolve after a few seconds is not announced, and appears in the next snapshot instead.

Events mined in the last ten minutes are replayed on subscribe, so a creation or settlement just before the watch went live is still announced. A replayed settlement is announced only for a market this subscription has seen, in the snapshot or as created; one the live watch delivers is announced regardless, since the snapshot may have dropped a market that settled while it was read.

Resolution comes from the settlement contract's MarketFinalized (voided flag and payout), joined to the module's by market key; one whose pair never arrives is not announced. Read `GET /v0/markets/{symbol}` for it.

AUTHENTICATED: the subscribe frame must carry a valid bearer token in `params.bearerToken`, and the stream is bound to that token's wallet — you cannot subscribe to another wallet's positions. Perpetual markets only.

PositionsUpdate.name: PositionsUpdate
PositionsUpdate.title: Positions Update
PositionsUpdate.description: One of your positions after it changed. `size`, `avgEntryPrice` and `realizedPnl` are the position's absolute new state, so replace the position wholesale rather than folding anything into it (a repeat carries the same state and is safe to reapply). A `size` of `0` means the position is closed — remove it from local state, the way a `0`-quantity order-book level is removed. The snapshot never carries a closed position (flat rows are excluded). Also emitted after a funding settlement or an auto-deleveraging on the position.

lossy: PositionUpdated is decoded to absolute state; FundingSettled and AutoDeleveraged carry a payment / a size reduction, so the position is re-read and its current state emitted (or a `0`-size removal when it has closed) — the settlement payment and the reduction amount themselves are not surfaced here. If the bounded wait for the indexer to reach the event's block times out, the re-read still runs and emits whatever state the indexer has reached; when that is still below the event, the change is reconciled by a bounded retry, a later event, or a resubscribe.

Funding / deleveraging events on one position are coalesced into fewer re-reads: an event arriving after a read has started may trigger a further read and update, so some intermediate states are not emitted (the count of updates is not one per event). Each update is absolute state, so a client replaces the position with whichever update it receives and loses nothing it tracks.

A market listed mid-subscription is resolved by an on-demand registry refresh when its first event arrives; only if that market stays unresolvable (e.g. the indexer cannot be reached) is the update dropped, reconciled on the position's next update or on resubscribe.

lossy: InertOrderCancelled is not watched: it reports an operator winding a registry down rather than a leg of this order's life.

outcome.description: Event-contract orders only: the outcome. `isBid` and `price` are in this outcome's terms.

chainId.description: The chain to subscribe on. Defaults to 50312, the only chain this deployment serves.

kind.description: Which market each symbol names when a spot and a perp market share it. Omitted, spot first, then perp, then event. A market's contract address in place of the symbol needs no kind. Part of the subscription: unsubscribe with the same kind.

symbols.description: Perpetual market symbols to subscribe to; deduplicated, at most 8 unique

limit.description: Max number of historical liquidation legs (default 100, at most 1000)

chainId.description: The chain to subscribe on. Defaults to 50312, the only chain this deployment serves.

bearerToken.description: A bearer token (a SIWE-issued JWT). The subscription streams only this token holder's own positions.

id.description: The leg's id, `${txHash}_${logIndex}` — the same key the REST endpoint reports, so a client can drop a leg it already holds after a reconnect.

kind.description: Which stage of the waterfall this leg is. Read it first: an `AutoDeleveraged` leg is otherwise indistinguishable from a `PositionLiquidated` one.

account.description: The liquidated account. On `AutoDeleveraged` this is the bankrupt account, not the counterparty who absorbed the position.

sizeDelta.description: Signed size for the leg; the sign is the side being closed.

markPrice.description: Mark price, takeover price or ADL bankruptcy price, depending on `kind`.

kind.description: The market's class, as `MarketInfo.kind` on REST.

contract.description: The market's contract address, as `MarketInfo.contract` on REST. With `kind`, it tells apart a spot and a perp market that share a symbol.

size.description: Signed position size: positive is long, negative is short. `0` means the position is closed — remove it from local state.

id.description: Client correlation id, echoed on the reply. Must be a JS-safe integer (|id| <= 2^53 - 1); a fractional or larger value is not echoed.
